title: Zapier in 2026: from 'connect two apps' to orchestrating the whole system
content:
Zapier built its name on the simplest idea in automation: when this happens, do that. For a decade that was enough. In 2026 it has repositioned hard, and the new label tells the story: it now calls itself an AI Orchestration Platform, not an app-connector.

What that actually means:

1. Zapier Agents. The headline shift. Instead of a fixed Zap that follows rules, an Agent is a goal-oriented teammate that can plan, reason, take actions, and adapt to context across 9,000+ apps. Agent templates now sit right next to Zap templates, so both models live in one place.

2. Copilot. An AI assistant that builds and edits workflows for you, so you describe what you want instead of wiring every step by hand.

3. An MCP server. The quietly important one: Zapier now exposes 30,000+ of its actions to external LLMs over MCP, so your own AI tools can call Zapier's whole catalog of integrations directly.

4. Governance baked in. AI Guardrails, Bring Your Own Model, and Memory. The pitch is no longer just connecting apps, it is orchestrating systems that mix AI, people, and data, with controls around them.

The honest trade-off: Zapier is still the easiest on-ramp and has the widest app coverage, but it is the priciest as you scale, which is exactly why teams comparing it to n8n and Make weigh cost against convenience.

So across this series: n8n gives you self-hosted control, Make gives you a visual agent canvas, and Zapier gives you the widest reach plus the smoothest AI layer, for a price.

Question for the group: for an AI-driven workflow today, would you reach for Zapier's polish, Make's visual agents, or n8n's control? And what is the deciding factor, cost, app coverage, or how much you self-host?
